messages.content: "Can you help me book a ticket for a concert of Taylor Swift in New York with a VIP Seating add-on, then book another ticket for a concert of Ed Sheeran in Los Angeles with a Backstage Pass and Parking Pass add-ons, and finally book a ticket for the Coachella festival in Indio with a Camping Pass and Parking Pass add-ons?"

function.name: concert_book_ticket
function.description: Book a ticket for a concert at a specific location with various add-ons like backstage pass. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

artist.description: Name of the artist for the concert.

location.description: City where the concert will take place.

add_ons.description: Add-ons for the concert. Default is 'VIP Seating' if not specified.

function.name: festival_book_ticket
function.description: Book a ticket for a festival at a specific location with various add-ons like camping access. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City where the festival will take place.

add_ons.description: Add-ons for the festival. Default is 'Camping Pass' if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants three bookings:

1) Concert of Taylor Swift in New York with VIP Seating.

2) Concert of Ed Sheeran in Los Angeles with Backstage Pass and Parking Pass.

3) Festival Coachella in Indio with Camping Pass and Parking Pass.

We have two functions: concert_book_ticket and festival_book_ticket. We need to call them accordingly.

Concert booking requires parameters: artist (string), location (city), optional add_ons which can be one or more from list? The type says add_ons?: "Backstage Pass" | "VIP Seating" | "Parking Pass"[]. That seems ambiguous but likely expects an array of strings maybe. For single add_on we could just provide as string? But default is VIP Seating if not specified. So first request: artist="Taylor Swift", location="New York". No add_ons needed because default is VIP seating; but they explicitly want VIP Seating so we might specify it anyway. Let's include add_ons=["VIP Seating"].

Second: artist="Ed Sheeran", location="Los Angeles", add_ons=["Backstage Pass","Parking Pass"]

Third: festival=Coachella, location=Indio, add_ons=["Camping Pass","Parking Pass"]. Since default is Camping Pass, but also want parking pass.

Thus produce calls sequentially. We'll use tool invocation format exactly. Probably separate lines each calling appropriate function. Use JSON arguments inside parentheses after function name. Ensure correct quoting. Provide all calls.
